evidence.title: Ohio Won’t Approve Weak High School Credentials

occurrences.checkable_against: Fordham Institute reports and district credential-use records
occurrences.quote_span: The Cleveland, Columbus and Cincinnati school districts, all flagged by Fordham as having large numbers of students using weak credentials
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce high school graduation credentials

occurrences.checkable_against: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce implementation schedule
occurrences.quote_span: the requirements would start with freshmen entering high school this fall
occurrences.speaker: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce
occurrences.subject: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce high school graduation credentials

occurrences.checkable_against: Ohio credential-point graduation rules and approved credential list
occurrences.quote_span: Ohio is also tightening how students can combine more than 700 approved, but lesser, credentials to earn enough credential “points” to graduate, a tactic that one expert described as “random acts of credentialing.”
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce high school graduation credentials

occurrences.checkable_against: Ohio student credential records and 2023 statewide employer-demand data for National Incident Management Systems credentials
occurrences.quote_span: In addition, more than 4,000 students earned a series of National Incident Management Systems credentials sought for fewer than 300 jobs that year.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce high school graduation credentials

occurrences.checkable_against: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce announcement or transcript
occurrences.quote_span: In announcing the list, Dackin conceded, “we know this is going to have a large impact on graduation rates.”
occurrences.speaker: Steve Dackin
occurrences.subject: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce high school graduation credentials

occurrences.checkable_against: Fordham Institute public statement or publication on Ohio's credential changes
occurrences.quote_span: The Fordham Institute, a non-profit education advocacy group active in Ohio, also praised the changes.
occurrences.speaker: Fordham Institute
occurrences.subject: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce high school graduation credentials

occurrences.checkable_against: The cited study of high-school credentials and employer demand
occurrences.quote_span: But concerns have grown in recent years over a mismatch nationally between what schools offer and businesses want, with one study estimating that only 18 percent of credentials earned by high school students matter to employers.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce high school graduation credentials

occurrences.checkable_against: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce credential application procedures
occurrences.quote_span: schools can apply to include other credentials
occurrences.speaker: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce
occurrences.subject: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce high school graduation credentials

occurrences.checkable_against: Statements from the Cleveland, Columbus and Cincinnati school districts and Fordham reports
occurrences.quote_span: The Cleveland, Columbus and Cincinnati school districts, all flagged by Fordham as having large numbers of students using weak credentials, also declined to address that question directly, other than to say they support having credentials that matter and that other credentials could be added later.
occurrences.speaker: Cleveland, Columbus and Cincinnati school districts
occurrences.subject: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce high school graduation credentials

occurrences.checkable_against: Ohio's revised credential-point list and bundle rules
occurrences.quote_span: Ohio has cut that list from more than 700 credentials to 126, available only as part of 21 pre-determined “bundles” of specific credentials in five fields — agriculture, business, construction, health care and manufacturing.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce high school graduation credentials

occurrences.checkable_against: Steve Dackin interview or statement and Ohio postsecondary/workforce plans data
occurrences.quote_span: Dackin said too many students are skipping college without having a plan to make a good salary.
occurrences.speaker: Steve Dackin
occurrences.subject: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce high school graduation credentials

occurrences.checkable_against: Historical Ohio approved-credential lists
occurrences.quote_span: “The intent was very strong a few years ago…but then their list ballooned to over 700 that students could earn. I think we’re just seeing the reckoning and the pendulum shift back.”
occurrences.speaker: Adriana Harrington
occurrences.subject: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce high school graduation credentials

occurrences.checkable_against: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce implementation guidance and application rules
occurrences.quote_span: The department would say only that the requirements would start with freshmen entering high school this fall, so schools have time to adjust, and that schools can apply to include other credentials, though they should meet standards for pay and employer demand.
occurrences.speaker: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce
occurrences.subject: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce high school graduation credentials

occurrences.checkable_against: Ohio high school graduation requirements and credential policy records
occurrences.quote_span: Ohio, since 2019, has made earning a credential that’s recognized by employers a key path to earning a diploma.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce high school graduation credentials

occurrences.checkable_against: Ohio Excels organizational records and methodology for evaluating Ohio credentials
occurrences.quote_span: Ohio Excels, a nonprofit created by the state’s major chambers of commerce, helped create the new list along with a way to evaluate each credential by how many students find jobs within a year, how much money they earn, whether a field is growing, and if the classes can count toward earning a college degree.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce high school graduation credentials

occurrences.checkable_against: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce credential list and state legislative records
occurrences.quote_span: In response and at the direction of the state legislature, the Ohio Department of Education and Workforce this summer cut its list of credentials that qualify students to graduate from 164 to 70.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce high school graduation credentials

occurrences.checkable_against: Ohio credential-point rules, student credential records and employer skill-demand data
occurrences.quote_span: That loophole let students seek easy and basic credentials scattered across different fields, such as drivers licenses, CPR and OSHA safety classes, without learning any skills deeply enough to matter to employers.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce high school graduation credentials

occurrences.checkable_against: Ohio credential attainment records and statewide employer job-demand data
occurrences.quote_span: In the most extreme case, about 9,000 students earned credentials wanted for just three jobs.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce high school graduation credentials

occurrences.checkable_against: Ohio's revised qualifying-credential list and annual credential-use/employer-demand data
occurrences.quote_span: The list notably drops two groups of credentials — one for retail sales and one for government management of emergencies — that several thousand students use each year to graduate despite little demand from employers.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce high school graduation credentials

occurrences.checkable_against: Fordham Institute reports and Ohio district credential and graduation records
occurrences.quote_span: Fordham has reported multiple times the last few years on ways some districts, notably urban, high-poverty ones where some students struggle to graduate, have large numbers of students earning low-value credentials just to earn a diploma.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce high school graduation credentials

occurrences.checkable_against: Ohio standalone credential list and labor-market wage data
occurrences.quote_span: Fordham’s Churchill said the state’s decision to include cosmetology licenses on the new list of standalone credentials despite low pay raises concerns for him.
occurrences.speaker: Fordham's Aaron Churchill
occurrences.subject: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce high school graduation credentials

occurrences.checkable_against: Ohio student credential records and 2023 statewide job-posting/employer-demand data
occurrences.quote_span: That system, Churchill and Fordham’s Jessica Poiner reported, had more than 9,000 students earning RISE UP retail sales and customer service credentials in 2023 — credentials that, combined, allow students to graduate — but were sought by employers for just three jobs statewide that year.
occurrences.speaker: Fordham's Aaron Churchill and Jessica Poiner
occurrences.subject: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce high school graduation credentials

occurrences.checkable_against: Ohio credential bundle specifications
occurrences.quote_span: Each bundle includes “foundational” credentials such as OSHA safety training, but only as first steps toward more advanced training.
occurrences.speaker: outlet's own
occurrences.subject: Ohio Department of Education and Workforce high school graduation credentials
